# Widget product guide

The front door answers with the guide lane (`agent/lib/widget-chat.ts`): one streamed `kbChat` call (google/gemini-3.6-flash, Google AI Studio first; `WIDGET_CHAT_MODEL` overrides it) with the product guide as a cached prefix, less the articles for pages the customer's features hide and the summary lines citing only those (one prefix per set of features off); a section gated inside a visible page stays, because the generator flattens it into the page, and the narrowing takes effect once a regenerated guide holds gated pages, started while the router scores the message and dropped on a handoff or a refund or ticket redirect. `WIDGET_CHAT=legacy` returns the front door to the help-center writer in `agent/lib/widget-kb.ts` for one release. The guide, `agent/lib/widget-product-guide.ts`, is generated from the help center with `pnpm widget:guide --repo <acquisity checkout> --ref <commit or branch>`. Retrieval, an article read tool and a grounding check after the reply were measured in rounds 2 to 4 and dropped: none lowered invented facts, and each cost time.

The guide regenerates on its own (ENG-15025). Acquisity's `docs-guide-trigger` workflow sends `docs-changed` with the commit SHA to this repository whenever `apps/web/content/docs/**` or `apps/web/lib/sidebar/catalog.ts` changes on its `main`, and `.github/workflows/widget-guide.yml` checks Acquisity out at that commit, runs the generator and opens or updates one PR on `bot/widget-guide` naming the commit, the regenerated sections and the model calls it made. It never merges: it files a `fixy`-labelled Linear ticket for the open PR, or reuses the open one (`scripts/generated-pr-ticket.ts`), and Fixy reviews and merges the PR (ENG-20297). Each model call's output is stored as data outside the bundled agent tree in `scripts/widget-product-guide.cache.json` under a hash of its model, prompt, sidebar and articles, so a rerun calls the model only for batches whose inputs changed (a sidebar catalog change changes every batch's prompt), and a run that changes nothing leaves the files as they were and opens no PR. The workflow runs generator code from trusted Foreman main, loads only validated JSON cache data from an existing bot branch, and skips committing or pushing when the result matches the pending PR. The cache is committed with the guide, so a run regenerates only the batches whose inputs changed; with an empty cache a run is a full bootstrap. Every call goes through the CLI Proxy, which reports no cost, so the run counts them as unpriced calls. The role and limit pass runs with thinking turned off: with it on, a full-guide summary spent its whole output budget reasoning (ENG-20607). On Gemini Flash it invented limits (ENG-20629). Automatic dispatches require a commit in Acquisity main history. Run the workflow by hand with an optional `sha` (default Acquisity `main`); set `allow_other_ref` explicitly to use a commit or ref outside main history, and `full` to regenerate every section; locally, `--full` does the same. Each batch has one three-attempt budget covering transport errors, truncation and invalid sections; terminal errors name the batch and failed runs write no partial guide. Logs and the PR body distinguish model attempts from successful responses and count the unpriced calls. A section, stored or new, that drops a UI label main's section for the same article quotes and the page still names, or says under four fifths of main's words, is distilled again on its own, asking for at least main's length with main's section as a reference, because a long article held to its word allowance can lose half its facts (ENG-21319). At most 12 such retries that need a model call run per run, worst first and in parallel, so a run that rewrites every section stays inside the job's time limit; a retry already stored costs nothing and doesn't count, and the next run takes the next worst. A retry is kept only when it drops no label the earlier section kept, and fewer of main's labels or more words. Its output stays cached while the section is still behind main, so a rerun makes no new call for a section it already retried. The PR body lists any section still behind main's. Checkouts retain no credentials, and documentation symlinks and paths outside the extracted docs tree are rejected. The availability and entry-point lines at the top of `scripts/widget-product-guide.ts` are checked in the app by hand, and the PR body says to recheck them when the catalog or `apps/web/lib/features.ts` changed. The sidebar, its opt-in pages and the settings menu are read from the app at the same ref, and a docs page or `<FeatureGate>` section behind an opt-in feature is marked "Only on workspaces where it has been turned on." (`agent/lib/widget-guide-gates.ts`). Secrets: Foreman needs `CLIPROXY_BASE_URL` and `CLIPROXY_API_KEY` (every model call), `LINEAR_API_KEY` (files the Fixy ticket) and `WIDGET_GUIDE_TOKEN` (reads Acquisity, pushes the branch and opens the PR on Foreman; the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot read the private Acquisity repo, and a PR it opens would not start `validate`), and Acquisity needs `FOREMAN_DISPATCH_TOKEN` (contents write on Acquisity/Foreman, which `repository_dispatch` requires).
